s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive visual impairment with endocrine dysfunction
salient_findings: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
key_facts: 2-week history of rapidly progressive visual reduction
Vestibular schwannoma treated by gamma-knife radiosurgery 2 years earlier
Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
Lesion predominantly isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images
Diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
Normal pituitary gland on MRI 2 years earlier

shortlist.label: Pituitary adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm with abnormal endocrine levels

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual reduction and endocrine dysfunction with a sellar/suprasellar mass

shortlist.label: Prolactinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated prolactin level and sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm

shortlist.label: Thyrotropic pituitary adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone level and sellar/suprasellar mass

shortlist.label: Non-functioning pituitary adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm with bitemporal hemianopsia

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of rapidly progressive visual reduction, bitemporal hemianopsia, and the presence of a sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm are consistent with a pituitary adenoma. The lesion's characteristics on MRI, including its isointensity to gray matter on T1-weighted images and hyperintensity on T2-weighted images with diffuse homogeneous enhancement, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Craniopharyngiomas are typically more heterogeneous and calcified on imaging, which is not described in this case

rejected.label: Prolactinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has an elevated prolactin level, the clinical presentation and imaging findings are not specific to prolactinoma

rejected.label: Thyrotropic pituitary adenoma
rejected.why: The abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone, free thyroxine, and free triiodothyronine levels could suggest a thyrotropic pituitary adenoma, but the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a non-functioning pituitary adenoma

rejected.label: Non-functioning pituitary adenoma
rejected.why: This is a possible diagnosis, but the presence of abnormal hormone levels and the patient's symptoms suggest that the tumor may be functioning to some extent, making pituitary adenoma a more general and encompassing diagnosis
